description:
The new StableYieldAccumulator is given an unbounded phlimbo approval that is hardcoded rather than mirrored from the retiring instance

Classification basis (verbatim from the severity-classifier): QA under C4: no assets at risk and no function or availability impact. It is a documented-standard deviation - the single Phase 5 value that breaks the phase's own 'read it off the live instance' discipline - which is precisely the QA tier.
impact: None. PhlimboV2 is a first-party contract and an infinite approval to it is the conventional pattern for a pull-based reward collector.
attackPath: 1. No attacker. Phase 5 mirrors the retiring accumulator's configuration field by field - `rewardToken`, `phlimbo`, `nftMinter`, `discountRate`, three `tokenConfigs`, three strategies, `nudgeSplit` - each read live off `OLD_SYA`.
2. One value is not mirrored: `sya.approvePhlimbo(type(uint256).max)` is a hardcoded infinite approval.
3. The inline comment justifies the mechanism ('collectReward pulls via transferFrom') but not the magnitude.
4. The project's own CLAUDE.md Configuration Safety section names caps and unbounded allowances as parameters requiring explicit justification rather than a default.
recommendation: Either read the retiring instance's existing phlimbo allowance and mirror it, or keep `type(uint256).max` and extend the comment to record why unbounded is correct here (PhlimboV2 is first-party, the approval is scoped to one spender, and `collectReward` is the only consumer) so the choice reads as deliberate rather than defaulted.
recommendationQuality: adequate - one sentence of justification is a legitimate and complete fix for a documentation-standard defect

severityDebate.why: Agrees with the proposed bucket; this pass simply makes the severity field consistent with it. Weakest candidate in the set. Retained rather than dropped because it is anchored to a WRITTEN in-repo standard (project CLAUDE.md Configuration Safety) rather than auditor preference, the fix is one sentence, and Phase 5 mirrors ELEVEN values off the live retiring instance while hardcoding exactly this one. Cached known-issue #10 ('admin trust assumptions…') was considered and rejected as authority - it has no suppression standing in this project (the declared known-issues file does not exist) and would fail on the merits anyway, since a discipline break against the repo's own written standard is not an admin-trust concession.
severityDebate.recallNote: Under Law 1, keep. A QA line item costs the report almost nothing, and dropping it would remove the only record that the discipline break was noticed.
